articles.title: The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This article provides a guide to observing celestial objects in the July sky, highlighting Saturn's details and offering tips for sketching, while also noting the visibility of Mercury, Neptune, Uranus, and Pluto. It commemorates Neptune's 165-year orbital anniversary and details the impressive six-year mission and scientific legacy of the Mars Spirit rover, which recently concluded operations.

articles.title: Photographs from the SJAA General Meetings
articles.summary: The article presents photographs and brief descriptions of two SJAA General Meetings. The December 18th meeting featured Dr. Tim Dubbs speaking on Particle Physics and his work on the LHC. The May 14th meeting hosted Dr. Jessie Christiansen from the SETI Institute, who discussed the latest results from the NASA Kepler Mission in the search for exoplanets, attracting approximately 50 attendees.

articles.title: Pictures Speak WISE
articles.summary: NASA's Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) mission has released new galactic images, captured using four narrow-band infrared filters (3.4 to 22 microns). These images primarily show light from warm dust, with blue areas indicating older stars and red/yellow areas signifying new star growth. The article highlights several galaxies like M51, M81, and M83, and mentions accompanying statistics and a trivia quiz.

articles.title: Descriptions of Deep Sky Objects
articles.summary: This document lists nine deep-sky objects, primarily galaxies, detailing their estimated distances and physical sizes. It also includes a trivia section featuring common names, unique characteristics, and historical observations related to these specific celestial bodies, prompting readers to identify them.

articles.title: The Last Month In Astronomy
articles.summary: This astronomy update from June 2011 covers several key events, including the controversial cancellation of the Terrestrial Planet Finder (TPF) and the conclusion of Space Shuttle Endeavour's final mission, which installed the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer. The article also highlights the end of the Mars Rover Spirit's operations, the discovery of numerous free-floating Jupiter-sized planets, and new observations of 'green rain' on a protostar by the Spitzer telescope. Additionally, it details the upcoming OSIRIS-REx asteroid sample return mission and new theories on Mars's rapid formation.

articles.title: It Must Be Astronomical...
articles.summary: This article from the SJAA Ephemeris newsletter covers various club activities and information. It details a telescope loaner program, announces a new Pentax GPS add-on for astrophotography, and presents statistics on numerous successful school star parties held throughout the year. The document also includes answers to a galaxy quiz, contact information for club officers and staff, and publication details for the newsletter.
